predecessors.name: Regency of Algiers
predecessors.text: the province of Constantine, which the Regency's Bey had governed as 'a provincial governorate' under 'the suzerainty of the Algerian Dey' since the 16th century

successors.name: French Algeria
successors.text: the province of Constantine, whose capital 'fell in 1837' ('The Beylik collapsed in the 1837 siege of Constantine'); 'The Constantine department was formed upon the bases of the Beylik in 1848'

ledger.x: 1830: the Constantinians rally to Ahmed Bey after Algiers falls.
1837: the rest of the province is left without a state.
1837: the Beylik of Constantine ends with the fall of its capital.

wars.name: Sieges of Constantine
wars.outcome: French victory at the second attempt: Clauzel's expedition of November 1836 was repulsed; the city fell in 1837, Damrémont having been killed and replaced by Valée.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the page gives the province's dimensions and its neighbours (Tunis on the east, Titteri on the west, the Sahara on the south) but no frontier.
